title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that exploited the visual trust created by an AI-generated website. The scammer used a real mobile trading app but overlaid it with a fake website displaying false account balances, creating the illusion of legitimate transactions and profits. The victims could see apparent gains and make small successful withdrawals, each step designed to deepen their confidence before requesting larger sums.

This is a failure of verification at the point where a user encounters financial information. The victims had no way to confirm that the account balances displayed on their screen were genuine rather than fabricated. The scam succeeded because AI-generated visual content created a complete illusion of legitimacy without any human verification step between the victims and the false information they were relying on to make financial decisions.

It is not established whether the mobile app itself had security measures that failed, or what role the app provider played in the scam's success.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, initially allowing him to make small trades and withdraw funds to build trust. Over time, the investments grew larger. When Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal, he discovered the scam. Police explained that while the app itself was real, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false account balances on his screen.

Jerry and Mindy Dunaway are now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. They say they feel angry, embarrassed, and financially devastated. Gwinnett County police are investigating the case, but authorities indicate that victims in these types of scams rarely recover their money. The couple's children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
